reviews.one_line_contribution: A pre-registered, paired-comparison study asking what fraction of a procedural-memory bank's accuracy gain over a hand-written instruction survives once a reflective prompt optimizer (GEPA) is trained on the exact same episodes, reporting a single substitution ratio S via a superiority-plus-TOST-equivalence conjunction, with a compiled-bank arm, a whole-bank-dump arm, a co-adaptation arm, and a deliberately non-compilable positive control to certify the instrument can detect non-substitutable value.
reviews.closest_prior_work: EvoAgentBench (arXiv 2607.05202), which the proposal itself surfaces and partially concedes to: it already runs Memento, ReasoningBank and GEPA on a shared 528/267 train/test split and reports that no automatic method wins in every cell. That paper establishes the exact three-way template (memory vs. optimizer vs. vanilla on matched trajectories) this proposal is built on, so it substantially narrows the novelty claim. What remains genuinely new is what EvoAgentBench structurally cannot compute — it has no combined optimizer+memory cell, so it cannot answer 'does the memory-vs-none gap shrink once the optimizer has seen the same data,' which is this proposal's actual object. That is a real, if incremental, advance layered on top of an already-published comparison.
reviews.strongest_objection: The track explicitly restricts scope to 'small open-weight models (7B-32B class)... the interesting result must not depend on frontier-scale models' and caps resources at 'open-weight models up to ~32B.' The proposal's primary, load-bearing agent A1 is gpt-oss-120b — roughly 4x over that ceiling — chosen specifically because it is where a prior study found a non-null memory effect. The one agent that is actually in scope, Qwen3.5-27B (A2), is pre-registered from the outset as the 'degenerate regime' where the bank has no effect at the hand-written instruction and S is explicitly undefined ('the question is moot'). So the only cells that can answer the paper's central hypothesis (H1∧H2 on A1) run on an out-of-scope model, while the track-compliant model is defined in advance to produce no answer at all. A strict area chair could reject on scope grounds alone, and there is no fallback in the design that tests the substitution claim on any 7B-32B agent where memory actually helps.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Identify or construct at least one 7B-32B-class agent/environment pairing where the ExpeL bank shows a genuine, non-degenerate effect (via the same G1/G6-style precheck already used to screen A1 and A2), and run the primary substitution test there, so the headline claim does not depend on stepping outside the track's stated model-size ceiling. Separately, build the memory artifact in the actual ReasoningBank format (self-judged success/failure distillation), not only ExpeL-style INSIGHT/PROCEDURE/OUTCOME items, since ReasoningBank is repeatedly named as a target system and is what the closest comparator (EvoAgentBench) actually evaluated — without it the reported numbers can't be cross-checked against that benchmark. Given the design already spans 14+ cells x 2 agents x 2 environments plus moderator, iso-cost, and generality analyses, also commit explicitly to the minimal subset that must ship even under the stated contingency cuts, so a reader can see the guaranteed core result independent of the extensions.
reviews.missing_baseline: A ReasoningBank-style bank (self-judged success/failure distillation over trajectories), as opposed to the ExpeL-style INSIGHT/PROCEDURE/OUTCOME bank actually built. ReasoningBank is named throughout as one of the 'target' systems and is central to the closest prior work (EvoAgentBench's own ReasoningBank cells), but the experiments never construct one, so the substitution ratio reported here cannot be directly compared to the closest published table's numbers — a reviewer would ask whether the substitution result is specific to ExpeL-style distillation or generalizes to the memory format the field actually benchmarks most.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is procedurally more rigorous than most: it states a dated scan, multiple verification channels (HF Papers queries, by-ID abstract checks, web search), and — unusually — documents a self-correction, reinstating five citations (including TERMS-Bench and MemAPO) that an earlier version of this proposal had wrongly retracted as unverifiable. It also directly names and engages the paper that most threatens novelty (EvoAgentBench, arXiv 2607.05202), withdrawing an explicit prior claim that 'no published work uses one as the control for the other.' That is exactly the behavior this instruction is meant to reward. That said, the check cannot be taken at face value: it cites roughly twenty very recent (2026 Q1-Q3) arXiv IDs with unusually precise statistics attached (e.g., '65.7% attributable to procedural anchoring,' 'retrieval precision collapsing from 29.6% to 3.3%'), none of which I can verify, and the process's own admission that a prior scan produced false retractions shows the method is not yet reliable. Net: the collision check is a real, substantive part of the submission rather than a pro forma gesture, but its central defense — that EvoAgentBench lacks the combined cells needed for a substitution test — is the load-bearing claim for this proposal's novelty and rests entirely on preprints I have no way to independently confirm.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A pre-registered, statistically rigorous test of how much of the accuracy gain from a retrieved procedural-memory bank (ExpeL-style, ReasoningBank-style) survives once a GEPA-optimized instruction is trained on the identical episodes, quantified as a substitution ratio S (superiority-at-baseline plus TOST-equivalence-at-optimized conjunction), with matched-token compiled-bank and whole-bank-dump control arms and a synthetic non-compilable positive control that must show low substitution to certify the instrument works.
reviews.closest_prior_work: EvoAgentBench (arXiv 2607.05202), which the proposal's own collision check surfaces and concedes is 'the three-way comparison v2 said did not exist': it already runs a memory retriever (Memento, ReasoningBank) and GEPA on a shared 528/267 training/test trajectory split across four domains and three backbones, and reports that no automatic method dominates every cell. The proposal's genuinely new material relative to it -- the combined optimizer+memory cells (I2xM1, I2xM0), the token-matched compiled and whole-bank arms, the coverage-matched bank, the substitution-ratio statistic with paired equivalence testing, and the B-dup positive control -- is real methodological machinery, but it is an instrumentation upgrade on an already-published table rather than a newly discovered phenomenon.
reviews.strongest_objection: The research-track brief this was written for requires 'Small open-weight models (7B-32B class)... The interesting result must not depend on frontier-scale models,' yet the primary, 'load-bearing' agent A1 is gpt-oss-120b, chosen explicitly because it is the one agent (of two tested in the cited pilot study) where the ExpeL bank showed a nonzero memory effect (+7.7pt); the in-scope Qwen3.5-27B model showed the same bank's effect as TOST-equivalent to zero and is demoted to a secondary 'degenerate regime' arm on a reduced grid (A2, condition 11 in the falsifiable predictions). This means that within the track's own declared model-scale scope, the phenomenon the whole study exists to explain -- memory helping, and whether that help survives prompt optimization -- is never actually observed; the central substitution claim is only testable by stepping outside the stated resource/scope envelope. Given that the related literature the proposal itself cites (EvoAgentBench's '+7 on Qwen backbones' for ReasoningBank) suggests an in-scope memory-positive setup exists, choosing to escalate to a 120B model instead reads as reaching for the agent scale that produces the desired effect rather than testing the claim where the track asked it to be tested.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Swap or supplement A1 with an in-scope 7B-32B agent that shows a genuine memory effect with a real memory method -- e.g., ReasoningBank on a Qwen-class backbone, which EvoAgentBench's own results (cited in this proposal's Related Work) already report as positive -- so the substitution question is answered inside the track's actual resource constraints rather than requiring escalation to a 120B MoE model. Separately, cut the combinatorial scope: 14 primary cells x up to 4 optimizer seeds x 2 agents x 2 environments x a LoRA-SFT arm x human-validated moderator labeling is closer to two or three papers' worth of experiments than the 'days, not weeks' the brief specifies, and trimming it (the proposal's own 'ordered contingency cuts' list is a good starting point for what to drop preemptively) would materially reduce execution risk.
reviews.missing_baseline: ReasoningBank (rather than ExpeL) evaluated on an in-scope Qwen-class (7B-32B) backbone, which the proposal's own cited source (EvoAgentBench) reports produces a real, non-null memory effect (~+7pt); the plan instead builds another ExpeL bank and escalates to an out-of-scope 120B agent to find a nonzero effect to substitute away, without ever showing that its central phenomenon exists on a model the track's brief actually licenses.
reviews.preprint_collision: This is a genuinely strong collision check, better than most: a dated scan (2026-09-03, with a prior 2026-08-21 pass noted), 15 HF Papers queries, by-id abstract verification for 54 arXiv IDs, cross-channel web-search corroboration where arXiv itself was unreachable, a committed log file, and -- most tellingly -- an honest retraction: on finding EvoAgentBench, the proposal withdraws its own prior claim that 'no published work uses one as the control for the other,' and separately reinstates five citations a previous version had wrongly dropped for being 'unverifiable.' That said, the check itself flags unresolved residual risk (NeurIPS 2026 camera-readies surfacing in October, a possible buried 'GEPA + memory' ablation in some systems paper's appendix) and commits only to re-running the scan before freeze and submission -- so the novelty finding is provisional, and the proposal's remaining novelty claim rests on a fairly narrow set of measurement additions (paired substitution ratio, compiled/whole-bank arms, positive control) layered on top of EvoAgentBench's already-published three-way table.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A pre-registered, statistically rigorous audit of how much of a frozen procedural-memory bank's accuracy gain over a hand-written prompt (measured on gpt-oss-120b via ExpeL-style retrieval) survives once a GEPA-optimized instruction sees the same training episodes, formalized as a substitution ratio S tested by a superiority+TOST-equivalence conjunction, with a token-matched compiled-bank arm and a deliberately non-compilable positive control to separate a true null from an underpowered one.
reviews.closest_prior_work: EvoAgentBench (arXiv 2607.05202), which the proposal's own collision check names as closest work: it already runs Vanilla, Memento, ReasoningBank, and GEPA on a shared 528/267 train/test split across four domains and three backbones — the exact 'memory vs. optimizer on the same trajectories' table this proposal exists to interrogate, and its headline finding (no automatic method wins in every cell; GEPA nearly matches a curated reference on one backbone) is cited here as motivation rather than as a competing result. What remains genuinely new relative to it is the combined I1xM1/I2xM1/I2xM0 cells, the token-matched compiled-bank arm C, the coverage-matched B_touched control, and the paired substitution-ratio statistics — real additions but incremental completions of an existing table rather than a new comparison in kind, published only two months before this proposal.
reviews.strongest_objection: The entire load-bearing test (H1 and H2 on A1) runs on gpt-oss-120b, a 120B-parameter model outside the track's stated resource envelope ('self-hosted inference on open-weight models up to ~32B... The interesting result must not depend on frontier-scale models'). A1 was picked specifically because an internal pilot found a non-null bank effect only there; Qwen3.5-27B (A2), the one agent actually inside the track's model class, is exactly where the bank's effect was null, so it is demoted to a 'degenerate regime' where S is not even computed (prediction 11). The paper's central, falsifiable claim is therefore never tested within the resource/scope boundary this track set for itself, and the agent choice reads as selecting the regime that guarantees a measurable effect rather than the regime the track asked for.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Make the primary, load-bearing grid run on an in-scope agent (7B-32B) where a genuine — even if smaller — bank effect at the hand-written instruction can be pre-registered, rather than making the compliant agent (Qwen3.5-27B) the 'degenerate' side case; add at least one genuinely self-editing memory system (e.g. a ReasoningBank-style online-distillation bank) alongside the frozen, built-once ExpeL bank B, since the track is titled 'Self-Editing Memory' and B/B-dup are static; and cite the internal pilot ('proposal (1)') and the litscan file as verifiable appendices rather than unpublished internal context the agent-selection and gate thresholds depend on.
reviews.missing_baseline: A dynamically self-editing memory bank (ReasoningBank-style distillation from self-judged successes/failures, or Mem0/A-MEM-style continual rewriting) is never built or tested; B and the B-dup positive control are constructed once from S_train and then frozen and hashed for the whole study. Given the track's own name and the fact that Related Work section (1) treats ReasoningBank as a peer target system, a reviewer would demand the substitution/compilation result be shown for at least one truly self-editing memory, since as written the finding could be specific to one static, non-self-editing bank-construction method rather than to the class of systems the track is about.
reviews.preprint_collision: Unusually rigorous for this genre: a dated fresh scan (2026-09-03), by-id verification for 54 arXiv IDs, and an explicit self-correction of a prior version's erroneous retraction of five citations, including an honest concession that the closest work (EvoAgentBench) already runs the three-way memory/optimizer comparison the earlier proposal draft claimed did not exist. But it is entirely self-reported and unverifiable here, and its own 'Residual risk' paragraph names the exact exposure a reviewer should weight heavily: 'a GEPA + memory ablation may exist in an appendix of a systems paper' — which is precisely the combined cell (I1xM1) claimed as the proposal's chief novel contribution. Given the field's admitted volatility, the check's real weakness is not thinness but the structural blind spot of keyword/HF-Papers scanning against an ablation buried in someone else's appendix or a not-yet-indexed ICLR 2027 submission.
